in_arabic.name: مَقصود
in_arabic.long_meaning: المَقصود هو الهدف المطلوب الذي يتم حبه وطموحاً في الحياة، وهو مصدر إلهام للشخص، ويتميز بالتفاني والاستقامة في العمل لتحقيق الرضا الله، وهو إسم يرتبط بالجود والكرم والشجاعة

in_urdu.name: مَقصود
in_urdu.long_meaning: مَقصود کا مطلب ہے وہ مقصد جس کے لئے انسان اپنی زندگی کو وقف کرتا ہے، اور جو کچھ انسان اپنے لئے پسند کرتا ہے، یہ نام شوق و خواہش کا ایک علامہ ہے، اور اس کا تعلق انسان کی شوق و خواہش کے جذبے سے ہے، اور یہ نام ہمیشہ انسان کے دل میں موجود ہوتا ہے، اور وہ ہمیشہ اس کے لئے کوشاں ہوتا ہے

in_hindi.name: मَقصूद
in_hindi.long_meaning: मَقसूद का अर्थ है जिसे हमें प्राप्त करना होता है, जिस पर हमारी शौकीनी होती है, और जिसकी प्राप्ति के लिए हम कोशिश करते हैं, यह नाम मुसलमानों में बहुत पसंद किया जाता है, और यह नाम इबादत और भक्ति का प्रतीक है, और इसे मुसलमान अपने बच्चों का नाम देते हैं ताकि वे भी उसे प्राप्त करने के लिए कोशिश करें

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, the name "Maqsud" holds an importance not just as a personal name but could also be used for significant places or events. It signifies design, intention, and purpose. It is a reminder that every action, every deed, and every word has an intended meaning or purpose in our lives and in the larger scheme of our existence. The name Maqsud can act as a constant reminder for us to strive towards our goals with determination, as each of our actions are a stepping stone towards our intended Maqsud - our ultimate destination in this life.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Maqsud" has deep spiritual implications as it relates to the direction of our soul towards its intended destination - Allah (God). In Islamic teachings, Maqsud refers to the goal of achieving Allah's satisfaction and His pleasure in our lives. It is a constant reminder that our ultimate desire and goal should be to fulfill the Will of Allah and to follow His guidance. By focusing on our Maqsud, we align ourselves with the greater purpose of creation, and by living in accordance with Allah's will, we maximize our potential for spiritual growth and development. Thus, "Maqsud" echoes the essence of Islamic belief, emphasizing the importance of living a purposeful and intentional life, guided by and ultimately aimed at Allah.

historical_references.reference: The Maqsud of Alhambra, a palace and fortress complex located in Granada, Spain, was built during the Nasrid Dynasty (1232-1492). The name 'Maqsud' is believed to have been given to denote the fortress's ultimate purpose: to protect and serve as a royal residence for the Nasrid rulers.
historical_references.context: Nasrid Dynasty, Alhambra, Spain, fortress, royal residence

historical_references.reference: The term 'Maqsud' also appears in the context of the Mughal Empire (1526-1857) in India. It refers to a mausoleum, built for the burial of the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb (r. 1658-1707), at the complex of the Lal Qila (Red Fort) in Delhi. The Maqsud-i-Azam, as it is also known, is considered an architectural masterpiece of the Mughal period.
historical_references.context: Mughal Empire, India, mausoleum, Emperor Aurangzeb, Lal Qila (Red Fort)
